key_insight: CNet shows that complex-valued neural networks trained with Wirtinger derivatives can use physics-native operations, like unitary Fourier transforms and Born-rule outputs, to solve learning tasks efficiently.
engineering_relevance: The framework provides a C++/CUDA foundation for building and optimizing complex-valued models, with checked kernels, FFT-based convolutions, and an inference mode suited to practical deployment.
method: Complex-valued deep learning with Wirtinger (CR-calculus) autodifferentiation
Causal Fourier mixer via Bluestein / chirp-z factorization for O(N log N) sequence modeling
evidence_signal: The abstract reports evaluations on character-level language modeling, radio-modulation classification (RML2016.10a), and coherent-diffraction imaging, with the complex model matching or exceeding a parameter-matched real FNet and converging in under half the training steps.
watch_item: Performance depends on correctly implementing and tuning complex operators and CUDA kernels, and the benefits may be task-specific rather than universal.
paper_title: CNet: A Complex-Valued Deep Learning Framework with Wirtinger Autodifferentiation and FFT--Hadamard Convolution
